hypothesis: Adding deterministic freshness and clock-skew metadata to the reviewed upstream snapshot will prevent hosts from silently treating stale provenance as current without expanding the companion's read-only authority.
heldOutChecks: a snapshot younger than 72 hours reports current
a snapshot exactly 72 hours old reports stale
a future observation reports clock-skew rather than current
an invalid observation timestamp fails closed
CLI changes output includes the deterministic freshness state and expiry
MCP ruvnet_changes exposes the same freshness metadata without adding write authority

memoryDecision.ruvectorWasm: defer until at least 100 sanitized provenance records support a leakage-free retrieval comparison with exact lookup
memoryDecision.gnn: reject for the current ten-project, six-change corpus unless a held-out graph task demonstrates at least ten percentage points of task-success gain

forecast.prediction: Within 90 days, agent-memory interfaces will increasingly require freshness and provenance state to keep retrieved evidence from influencing actions after it expires.
forecast.falsifiableCriterion: By 2026-12-13, at least two primary agent-memory implementations or interoperability specifications expose explicit temporal freshness, expiry, or invalidation metadata in a public interface.
